content.title: Building Code Adoption: Significant Changes
content.summary: Significant changes to the Building Code are set to be adopted in 2026, including new provisions for special inspector registration, contractor licensing, and the construction of accessory dwelling units (ADUs) by homeowners. The 2024 International Residential Code will feature reorganized chapters for clarity, updated requirements for energy systems, and new regulations for sprinkler systems in new residential buildings. Additional changes include adjustments to stairway requirements, permitting processes for accessory structures, and the introduction of provisions for tiny houses and 3D printed homes.
content.body:
Below is a list of anticipated impactful changes coming with the new Building Code adoption in 2026. Please note that these changes are still under review.

## Significant administrative changes

- Adding special inspector registration provisions
- Changing contractor licensing letter designations for clarity and to align with other municipalities
- Allowing ADU’s to be built by a homeowner/occupant
- Updated language in our administrative provisions for expiration of permits to help clarify these provisions and help with flexibility in being able to provide extensions on permits where possible

## The 2024 International Residential Code (IRC) significant changes

- Chapter 3 reorganization- so that structural and fire-resistance provisions appear first, followed by smoke and CO detection and sprinkler requirements
- Sections covering room and space layout, egress, accessibility, and indoor environmental provisions are now arranged in a clearer, more intuitive order
- Requirements for solar and on‑site energy systems are grouped at the end to streamline navigation.
- IRC Appendix Reorganization: Appendices were renumbered and reordered to create a more logical structure with new groupings and names for appendixes
- New stairway changes; existing stairways being remodeled do not have to comply with current code requirements where the exceptions are applicable and compliance is not possible otherwise
- New Appendixes adopted: Tiny houses, ADU’s, 3D Printed homes and recommended procedures for inspection of existing appliances
- New ADU provisions will allow for more affordable and practical options for compliance with fire separation including new option for interconnection of smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in lieu of fire separation
- Removing previous amendment requiring exhaust fans regardless of operable windows
- Accessory structures permitting changes. A permit is now required for accessory structures over 120 sf, instead of 200 sf
- Ice barriers required in all parts of Arvada
- Fire separation requirements clarified for townhouses and ADUs and buildings on the same lot have been clarified
- Duplex allowance for stacked units
- Sleeping Lofts are now permitted
- Greater incentives for sprinkler systems built into code such as allowance to not be required to provide egress windows in basement sleeping rooms where a home is sprinklered, reduction of 2-1 hour rated party walls between townhome units and no more structural independent foundations required, the ability to build larger sleeping lofts and habitable attics without triggering a fourth story and allowances to build closer together without rated assemblies
- Chapter 11 for energy code will be deleted and replaced but the Model Low Energy Carbon Code- Based on the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code (LECC), residential provisions
- Sprinkler systems will now be required in new single family homes, townhomes and duplexes built per the IRC. This will not affect existing structures, additions or remodels.
- Updating language for current amendment for requirements for soils reports and design professional stamped foundation plans, allowing greater flexibility and options rather than a soils report in most scenarios
- Stairway/ Landing changes: Garage interior landings at doors can now be up to 7 ¾” below the door's threshold. A top landing is not required for stairways of not more than two risers, when at exterior doors. Where not serving the required egress door exterior stairways to grade with three or fewer risers only need a 36” wide landing at the bottom, regardless of the stairway's width. Alterations to existing stairways are no longer required to comply with the requirements for new stairs in certain situations
- Section M1411 Refrigerants: This section now includes provisions for the use of the new A2L refrigerants, which are becoming available for residential installations.

## The 2024 International Building Code (IBC) significant changes

- Updated wind, earthquake, and snow load provisions (no changes proposed to current design criteria, just updated provisions added for lessons learned)
- Openings in Shaft Enclosures: Additional exceptions are provided for shaft enclosures, including new allowances for openings and penetrations.
- Vapor retarders: changes provide additional options and better guidance for allowable types and locations of permitted vapor retarders
- Power operated doors for accessibility are now added as requirement
- Clarification of accessibility  requirements for R-3 occupancies
- Using the 2017 ICC A117.1 Code (newest ANSI accessibility code)
- 67” radius now required for wheelchair turning space due to changes in wheelchair sizes
- Adult changing tables now have regulations
- Dispersion of accessible units amongst types of units for accessibility now clarified
- Various code changes to align with fire code
- Updating language for current amendment for requirements for soils reports and design professional stamped foundation plans, to provide greater flexibility and options for cost savings

## The 2024 International Plumbing Code (IPC) significant changes

- Deleting chapter 14 for gray water
- Restrooms need not be provided for each sex when restrooms are provided for all persons regardless of sex
- Updated requirements for plumbing fixtures in Group I occupancies and Ambulatory care facilities
- New minimum standards for various plumbing piping materials and other materials
- New materials and plumbing products that promote water conservation

## The 2024 International Mechanical Code (IMC) significant changes

- Addition of a new minimum landing at the roof hatch for personnel to safely use the hatch when accessing the roof for repair and maintenance.
- Addition of a new testing option for grease ductwork
- Refrigerant updates: Addition of Group A2L and B2L refrigerant provisions and updates added from Arvada to better address these refrigerants and their needs for proper installation

## The 2024 International Fuel Gas Code (IFGC) significant changes

- Requiring calculations and details to be provided to show compliance with combustion air, dilution air and ventilation as part of construction documents

## The 2024 International Existing Building Code (IEBC) significant changes

- Adult changing station provisions now added
- Clearer language for changes to areas containing primary function
- Occupiable roofs have been built into various sections of the code
- Assists with clarifying how risk categories should be assigned for structural design
- Exterior wall covering and wall envelope changes
- Owner's responsibility at construction sites has been added to show the importance of developing, implementing and maintaining a site safety plan during construction

## The 2024 International Property Maintenance Code (IPMC) significant changes

- Deleting 45 municipal amendments that were made to our previous adopted 2009 version of this code.
- Clothes dryer exhaust duct maintenance required to prevent a leading cause of fires for homes and properties

## The 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code (ISPSC) significant changes

- Clarification of means of egress to include all public swimming pools vs just outdoor public swimming pools
- Clarification and strengthening requirements for plumbing fixture counts for all public swimming pools to better assist with public health
- Adds screen enclosures as barrier method

## The Colorado Model Low Energy Code, based on the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC), significant changes

- A new Colorado Low Energy Carbon Code book has been developed which is available for purchase through ICC. This will mean we will be able to utilize one code book to reference instead of both of these codes because the energy code will be combined with the LECC.
- NOT Penalizing gas/ fuel burning appliances, the code will now just make it easier for electric building to comply
- In the 2024 IECC alone, solar panels are required but this has been removed under the LECC which can drastically help reduce costs - on site renewables
- Improve design flexibility
- Estimate increase of 7-8% for efficiency relative to previous code cycle
- More energy conservation measures, including updated insulation standards and requirements for high-efficiency appliances
- Updates to different paths of compliance, providing additional clarity and flexibility with methods. Such as allowing an "F" factor for slabs so that they can be traded off when using a performance type method
- Additional options now for air leakage testing based on the method of compliance
- R403- Duct systems/ ductwork systems have added provisions and clarifications- such as for heat recovery or energy recovery ventilation systems. Aids in creating a balanced system and energy loss
- Additional auto-off features for lighting
- More efficient windows, skylights, and air sealing requirements
- EV Ready Provisions: Requires residential and commercial buildings to have infrastructure for EV charging
- Some provisions to install EV based on number of parking spaces
- Electric Ready Provisions: Dedicated electrical infrastructure
- Solar Ready Provisions: Requires single-family homes to have roofs designed for solar panels
- More flexible duct leakage requirements
- Allows limited trade-offs for heating, cooling, and water heating equipment that are more efficient than the federal minimum
- A system of credits in addition to mandatory provisions (R402-R404): A total of 51 measures available (each measure is not necessarily applicable in all climate zones, and some are mutually exclusive). Specific number of credits for each measure by climate zone. Must achieve a minimum of ten (10) credits. Must implement at least two (2) measures. Starts with a table of measures and credits and then followed by additional text further explaining measure requirements

## The 2024 International Fire Code (IFC) significant changes

- Operational Permits
  - Lithium-Ion batteries
  - Sky lanterns
  - Temporary sheltering
  - Valet trash
- Rural Fire Apparatus Access Roads
  - Mostly taken from Jefferson County Road and Transportation Manual
  - Allows for roads narrower than the prescriptive fire code and city roadway standards
- Driveways
  - Typical driveways not allowed for fire apparatus access.
- Open Burning
  - Prohibited in WUI areas unless portable fireplaces, recreational fires, and vegetation management.
  - Provided a list of prohibited materials to be burned
- Sky Lanterns
  - Additional provisions
- Retroactive Manual Fire Alarm Systems
  - Allow interior corridor R-2’s to meet exemption
  - Increased number of units from 16 to 24 to be exempted
- Stairwells In Buildings Under Construction
  - Changed it to be required at 20’ rather than 40’
- Fire Flow Requirements
  - Went back to prescriptive reduction of 75% for sprinklered buildings
- Fire Apparatus Access Roads – Loading
  - Increased from 85k pounds to 90k pounds
- Valet Trash
  - Added the requirement that this can only be done in a sprinklered building

## New Wildfire Resiliency Code/Wildland Urban Interface Code (WUIC) significant changes by adopting

- New buildings and structures will require compliance with this code where in a wildfire zone
- Additions will require compliance with this code
- Accessory structures over 120 sf will require compliance with this code
- Re-roofing that includes replacing over 25% of the roof covering will require compliance with this code
- Siding replacements that involves replacing over 25% of the exterior siding material will be required to comply with the siding material for this code and will also be required to comply with some defensible space requirements for this code
- A wildland urban interface map is being developed for Arvada that will be used to identify fire intensity classification areas. At this time, we are proposing to utilize Jeffco’s wildfire map for Arvada.
- Zone 1 (lower risk):
  - Certain types of windows, doors, roofing, siding, and fencing may be required.
  - Certain types of deck materials may be required, along with underfloor enclosures.
  - Mulch, shrubs, and small trees within 5 feet of buildings may need to be removed.
  - No new trees may be planted within 5 feet of buildings.
  - Trees should be pruned away from buildings.
  - Trees and shrubs within 30 feet of buildings should be spaced several feet apart.
  - No flammable debris or slash should be stored within 30 feet of buildings.
  - Planting of new juniper plants will be prohibited.
- Zone 2 (higher risk):
  - In addition to the above Zone 1 requirements, additional requirements would include:
    - More fire protections may be required, including protection of eaves and soffits and exterior door requirements for thickness.
    - Trees and shrubs within 100 feet of buildings should be spaced several feet apart.
    - No flammable debris or slash should be stored within 100 feet of buildings.
